summary: @servicetitan/suppress-warnings 38.1.3 preinstall fetches Bun and runs obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads a Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods the extracted binary executable, then execFileSyncs it against the shipped sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727 KB Bun-tagged JavaScript file (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) heavily obfuscated with string-array rotation (function WV8StW over the mixed const array n7gIxM) and a permuted base64 alphabet decoder (hc1jfK9); its cleartext behavior is not inspectable without executing it. The advertised purpose of the package is suppressing React development warnings, and the dist/ library code is a small benign React helper with no relation to the preinstall flow. Fetching a second language runtime at install time and using it to execute a large opaque sibling script matches the alternate-runtime-dropper shape used to evade Node-focused scanners, and the @servicetitan namespace has been affected by the Shai-Hulud npm worm family. Installing this version runs attacker-controlled obfuscated code under a freshly downloaded interpreter on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
